t.1.188.1: Then all the Pāṇḍavas and the illustrious Pāñcālya, seeing the great-souled Kṛṣṇa, rose to greet him and paid him honor.
t.1.188.2: Having greeted them all in return and at last asked after their welfare, that great-minded one sat down upon a shining golden seat.
t.1.188.3: Permitted by Kṛṣṇa of boundless splendor, all of them, the best of men, sat down on very costly seats.
t.1.188.4: Then, after a moment, Pārṣata, the lord of the people, uttered sweet words and questioned that great-souled one on Draupadī's behalf.
t.1.188.5: How can one woman be the wife of many, and yet there be no confusion of dharma? Let the blessed one tell us all this exactly as it is.
t.1.188.6: Concerning this law, which is deceptive and contrary to both the world and the Veda, I wish to hear whatever opinion each one of you holds.
t.1.188.7: Drupada said: This, in my view, is unrighteous, opposed to both the world and the Vedas; for one wife is not found among many husbands, O best of the twice-born.
t.1.188.9: Therefore I do not make such a resolve regarding this act, for this appears to me doubtful, clouded by uncertainty about dharma.
t.1.188.10: O bull among the twice-born, O brahmin rich in austerities, how could an elder brother, being of good conduct, approach the wife of his younger brother?
t.1.188.11: But because of the subtlety of dharma, we do not know its course in any way at all; whether this is adharma or dharma, no firm decision can be reached.
t.1.188.8: Nor was this dharma ever practiced by the great-souled ancients; and a dharma that stands divided in many ways is not to be followed as the eternal dharma.
t.1.188.13: My speech has never uttered a falsehood, nor is my mind set upon adharma; and my mind is inclined toward this, so this is in no way adharma.
t.1.188.12: It is not a thing for men such as us to do, O brahman; therefore I cannot in any way resolve that Kṛṣṇā should become the queen of five.
t.1.188.15: They say that the word of one's elder is the law, O best of those who know the law; and of all elders, the mother is the supreme elder.
t.1.188.14: For it is heard even in the Purāṇa, O best of those who uphold dharma, that a woman of the Gautama line named Jaṭilā dwelt with seven seers as her husbands.
t.1.188.17: It is just as this Yudhiṣṭhira, who walks in dharma, has said. I have a fierce fear of falsehood; how may I be freed from falsehood?
t.1.188.16: And she too spoke the words, “Let it be enjoyed like alms.” Therefore I consider this to be dharma, O best among the foremost of the twice-born.
t.1.188.19: As this dharma has been ordained, and since it is eternal, and as the son of Kuntī has declared it, so is the dharma; there is no doubt.
t.1.188.18: You will be freed from falsehood, good lady, and this is the eternal dharma. But I shall not speak of it before everyone; O Pāñcāla, hear it from me yourself.
t.1.188.20: Then the blessed lord Vyāsa Dvaipāyana rose and, taking the king by the hand, entered the royal palace.
t.1.188.21: The Pāṇḍavas, Kuntī, and Dhṛṣṭadyumna Pārṣata, their minds bewildered, remained right there, waiting for those two.
t.1.188.22: Then Dvaipāyana explained to that great-souled lord of men how it is dharma for many men to have a single wife.
